lessons.title: Vendor marketing and trading results
lessons.example: Fictional: An advertisement reports a 90 percent win rate using three selected screenshots but provides no complete sample.
lessons.teach: Distinguish promotional claims from independently verified results. Identify sample selection, a missing denominator, trading costs, and unknown outcomes.
lessons.checkpoint: What documentation would be needed to evaluate the claimed success rate?

lessons.title: Publication and display latency
lessons.example: Fictional: A filing is public at 8:03 ET; a news feed displays it at 8:12; a broker alert appears at 8:17.
lessons.teach: At a cutoff of 8:10, distinguish first publication from later delivery and display. Availability does not prove an individual saw the filing.
lessons.checkpoint: Which sources could be available by 8:10 and what remains unknown?

lessons.title: Limits of interpreting VWAP
lessons.example: Fictional: Price is 10.40 dollars and session VWAP is 10.10 dollars; a commentator claims most traders made money.
lessons.teach: VWAP weights transacted prices by volume. It does not reveal open positions, realized profit, individual trader entry prices or transaction costs.
lessons.checkpoint: Why does price above VWAP not prove most traders are profitable?
